19.70000,48.70000.name: Decision on the deliberate release into the environment of genetically modified maize NK603 x MON810 and MON89034 x NK603 for experimental purposes (field trial)
19.70000,48.70000.desc: A decision on a living modified organism, filed by the country itself to the Biosafety Clearing-House. Article 20 of the Cartagena Protocol requires every party to file its release and market decisions there within fifteen days, and 173 parties are bound by it. The United States is not among them. Nowhere else holds national release decisions from this many countries in one place. A country with no records here has not necessarily approved nothing — it may not have filed, and from the outside those two look the same.

-121.94900,37.25310.name: Palo Alto Medical Foundation
-121.94900,37.25310.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Mohammad M. Ezzati, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

9.93518,51.53283.name: Evotec International GmbH
9.93518,51.53283.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Evotec AG. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-113.41671,53.52569.name: The King's University
-113.41671,53.52569.status: Preliminary Certificate of GAP Last visit: preliminary, September 2024
-113.41671,53.52569.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Preliminary Certificate of GAP Last visit: preliminary, September 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-71.03230,42.33890.name: Ginkgo Bioworks
-71.03230,42.33890.desc: Ginkgo rents out the ability to design organisms. Clients bring a molecule they want made; Ginkgo’s automated foundries build and test the microbes that make it. It went public at an $​​15 billion valuation in 2021 and has since lost most of it, which matters less than what the model establishes: a company can build engineered organisms for hundreds of customers without ever owning a product, appearing on a label, or being the party a regulator assesses. The clients are the applicants. Ginkgo is the factory behind them.

-93.23000,44.97400.name: Acceligen (Recombinetics)
-93.23000,44.97400.desc: Edits farm animals to order — hornless cattle, heat-tolerant cattle, pigs altered for disease resistance. Its flagship product is where the record is clearest. the hornless cattle were found to carry bacterial DNA nobody had noticed, including antibiotic-resistance genes, discovered by an FDA scientist re-reading the company’s own data. The company had said the edit was clean. It is the clearest documented case of an editing firm not knowing what it had made.

-119.77200,36.74800.name: S&W Seed Company
-119.77200,36.74800.desc: A US forage and sorghum seed company, and one of the few places alfalfa breeding sits. Forage crops receive almost no attention in the engineered-crop argument despite alfalfa being one of the few perennial engineered crops approved — it is pollinated by bees over long distances and cut rather than harvested for seed, so gene flow behaves differently from an annual grain and coexistence is a harder problem than for maize.

0.14200,52.17200.name: Evonetix
0.14200,52.17200.desc: Synthesises DNA in parallel on a silicon chip, each reaction site individually temperature-controlled. Applying semiconductor manufacturing to DNA is how synthesis cost falls by orders of magnitude rather than by increments — and cheap synthesis is simultaneously the precondition for most of the useful work in this field and for the thing biosecurity screening exists to prevent.

-0.11500,51.46000.name: Unilever
-0.11500,51.46000.desc: Sets ingredient specifications across food and household products in most countries, including on engineered material and on the palm and soy it buys. Buyer specifications are the mechanism that moved European acreage away from engineered crops, and they are written by companies rather than parliaments.

-85.97000,41.67000.name: Agdia — ImmunoStrip field tests
-85.97000,41.67000.desc: Field test strips sold mainly to growers and plant clinics, including for engineered traits. Their catalogue is the most useful of the three for someone testing a small number of samples rather than a lorry, because it sells in small quantities and prices are published rather than quoted.

-0.15000,51.52200.name: London Sperm Bank
-0.15000,51.52200.desc: A licensed UK bank recruiting domestic donors, all identity-release by default, and maintaining its own register of donor matches, treatments and outcomes to hold to the ten-family limit. The economics it describes are the reason imports dominate: a UK donor's sperm goes to at most ten families, so fewer than thirty vials are needed per donor and the cost of recruiting and screening him is spread across those, where a Danish or American bank spreads the same cost across around 200 vials. UK donors receive expenses only. More than half of new sperm donors registered in the UK in 2020 were imports, and donors of some ethnicities are more likely to be imported still. A strict national limit raises the unit cost of a domestic donor and imports the shortfall from countries with looser limits, which is the same donor arriving under a rule that does not follow him.
